text:
alex_support: Customer onlineshop Inc reports repeated 429s when they run ingestion jobs against rwd-3. They say it spikes when they switch to 64k context windows and do a short fanout. They run ~40 concurrent requests, each request ~50-60k tokens. Asking if this is RPM/TPM per-model, concurrency, or something auth/billing related.

maria_engineer: Thanks — can you paste a sanitized curl + the exact response headers and the endpoint (text/generate vs chat) so we can triage? Also the org id if possible.

alex_support: Pasting sanitized repro (customer removed PII):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ***" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-3","input":"<~55k tokens payload>","stream":false}'
```
Response headers on failure:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 1
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1719456820
X-RWD-Model: rwd-3
```
They see bursts of 429s for ~30s then it clears. first_message_ts/req ids: req-abc123, req-abc124.

ken_sre: My quick read — long contexts multiply token throughput so they may be hitting token-per-minute (TPM) for rwd-3, or per-model RPM thresholds because each request is heavy. Also concurrency limits per model can be lower for high-memory configs. 429s are returned when either quota (TPM/RPM) or max concurrency is exceeded.

luis_billing: Also check account-level quotas. If they have a hard quota on tokens/min or per-model capacity, billing will block additional requests. Console -> Usage -> Quotas shows if they hit a limit.

priya_support: Do they use Hosted or Dedicated? If Dedicated, we can bump capacity for them. If Hosted, recommend reducing parallelism or requesting a quota increase.

maria_engineer: Quick repro steps to isolate root cause: 1) send the same payload serially (1 concurrency) — if no 429s, it's concurrency. 2) reduce context length (trim system + history) — if no 429s, it's TPM. 3) try a smaller model variant (rwd-3-medium) to see if it behaves. Also add exponential backoff with jitter.

ken_sre: Small script to reproduce serial vs parallel (sanitized):
```bash
# sequential
for i in {1..20}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"rwd-3","input":"<~55k tokens>"}' &> /dev/null
  sleep 0.2
done

# parallel (simulates customer)
for i in {1..40}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"rwd-3","input":"<~55k tokens>"}' &
done
wait
```
If sequential succeeds and parallel fails -> concurrency/quota hit. If both fail -> probably TPM (tokens/min) or malformed auth.

alex_support: I ran step 1 with them — sequential (1 at a time) completed fine. Parallel at 40 concurrent reproduces 429s within ~10s. Customer wants to keep ~40 concurrency for throughput. Is there a config to allow that?

maria_engineer: Short answer: we can request a per-model quota bump for that org but it's not automatic — need infra approval. Longer: recommended mitigations — lower concurrency, do chunked batching (split large context into smaller chunks and stream/concatenate), enable prefix caching if much of the context repeats, or move to Dedicated where you reserve capacity. Also ensure client uses exponential backoff and respects Retry-After header.

luis_billing: I'll check org quotas and open a temporary quota increase if justified. Please provide org id + usage graphs. A note: even with a quota bump TPM still scales with tokens, so 40x very-large-context reqs will be expensive.

maria_engineer: I'll open an infra ticket to evaluate short-burst capacity and whether we can increase per-model concurrency window for rwd-3 for that org. Also logging note: add token usage per-request to logs (we already have it) so we can prove TPM vs concurrency.

alex_support: thanks — sharing graphs and org id with Luis + infra ticket id when available. Customer accepted immediate workaround: reduce concurrency to 5 and use chunking.

rwd-deploy-bot: Created ticket INF-1234 (increase per-model burst for org: onlineshop-inc) and linked to billing case BILL-987.

alex_support: Update: ran tests again with onlineshop — setting concurrency to 5 eliminated 429s; chunked ingestion and request for quota bump in flight. Customer happy to iterate. Closing this support thread unless infra asks for more logs. :white_check_mark:
